The following code should do what you want. It uses melt and
strsplit:

library(reshape2)
library(plyr)

df <- data.frame(path=1:5,
a.1=rnorm(5),
a.2=rnorm(5),
bbnum.25=rnorm(5),
dd.4.50=rnorm(5),
eee.31.5=rnorm(5))


split_at_period <- function(x){
tmp <- strsplit(as.character(x), "\\.")[[1]]
data.frame(t1=tmp[1],
t2=tmp[2],
t3=tmp[3])
}


# melt df
mdf <- melt(df, id.vars="path")

# use ply
pdf <- data.frame(path=mdf$path,
ldply(mdf$variable, split_at_period),
value=mdf$value)
pdf

I haven't followed this thread closely, but thought I would point out
that the reshape2 package has a colsplit function. colsplit() works
like this:

my.df <- data.frame(path=1:5,

a.1=rnorm(5),
a.2=rnorm(5),
bbnum.25=rnorm(5),
dd.4.50=rnorm(5),
eee.31.5=rnorm(5))

mydf.m <- melt(mydf, id.vars="path")

pdf2 <- cbind(mydf.m, colsplit(mydf.m$variable, pattern="\\.",
names=c("t1", "t2", "t3")))

best,
Ista
